title: Elementary Mathematics III (Vectors, Geometry and Dynamics)
description: The analytical geometry and mechanics course, taught as MAT 141: Analytical Geometry and Mechanics before the CCMAS codes: coordinate geometry of lines, circles and polar coordinates, conic sections, vectors and their products, lines and planes in space, kinematics and projectiles, and dynamics with moment of inertia. Built from the MAT 141 slides of Dr B. O. Onasanya and Dr O. B. Ogunfolu and the 2016 lecture note, and the papers from 2021/22 to 2025, labelled with the former code.

topics.title: Coordinate Geometry of Lines
topics.summary: Plane coordinate geometry measures distances, divides segments in a ratio and describes straight lines by their slopes and equations. It also finds perpendicular distances from a point to a line and the angle between two lines.
subtopics: Distance between two points
Dividing a line in a ratio; the midpoint
Slope of a straight line
Forms of the equation of a line
Parallel and perpendicular lines
Perpendicular distance and the angle between two lines

topics.title: Circles and Polar Coordinates
topics.summary: A circle is the set of points at a fixed distance from a centre. Its equation, centre and radius, and its tangents and normals, follow from that definition, and polar coordinates describe points by distance and angle.
subtopics: Standard equation (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r²
General equation x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0
Tangent and normal at a point
Circles touching lines; length of a tangent
Circle through three points
Cartesian and polar coordinates

topics.title: Conic Sections
topics.summary: Conic sections are the curves cut from a cone by a plane: the circle, parabola, ellipse and hyperbola. Each is the locus of a point whose distance from a focus is e times its distance from a directrix, and each has standard equations, tangents and normals.
subtopics: Eccentricity, focus and directrix
The parabola y² = 4ax
The ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1
Ellipses with shifted or vertical axes
The hyperbola x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 and its asymptotes
Tangents and normals to conics

topics.title: Vectors and Their Products
topics.summary: A vector has magnitude and direction and is written with the unit vectors i, j and k. The scalar product gives angles, projections and work done, and the vector product gives perpendicular vectors, areas, moments and, with a triple product, volumes.
subtopics: Scalars and vectors; magnitude and unit vectors
i, j, k notation, position and displacement vectors
Direction cosines; collinear and coplanar points
The scalar product: angles, projections and work
The vector product: areas and moments
The scalar triple product and the ratio theorem

topics.title: Lines and Planes in Space
topics.summary: In three dimensions a line is fixed by a point and a direction vector, and a plane by a point and a normal vector. Students write their vector, parametric and Cartesian equations and find intersections and distances.
subtopics: Vector equation of a line r = a + αd
Line through two points
Parametric and standard Cartesian forms
Intersection of two lines
Equation of a plane n·(r − r₀) = 0
Plane through three points; line meeting a plane

topics.title: Kinematics and Projectiles
topics.summary: Kinematics relates displacement, velocity and acceleration by differentiation and integration. Students solve straight-line motion with variable acceleration, distance versus displacement, motion in space, and projectiles under gravity.
subtopics: Displacement, velocity and acceleration as derivatives
Velocity and displacement by integration
Distance travelled versus displacement
Constant acceleration and free fall
Projectile motion: components, greatest height, time of flight, range
Motion in space with position vectors

topics.title: Dynamics, Relative and Circular Motion, and Moment of Inertia
topics.summary: Dynamics links forces to motion through Newton's laws, momentum and work. MAT 141 also covers relative velocity, circular motion with angular velocity and acceleration, elastic strings, and the moment of inertia of rods and plates.
subtopics: Newton's laws, resultant forces and F = ma
Momentum, impulse, work and power
Relative position, velocity and acceleration
Circular motion: angular velocity, normal and tangential acceleration
Elastic strings and Hooke's law
Moment of inertia, radius of gyration and the parallel axes theorem
